title: Log in to the university portal to confirm your details
scenario: An email link opens a login page that looks exactly like your university's portal, asking you to confirm your username and password after a routine security check.

answers.A: Log in since the page looks identical to the real portal.
answers.B: Log in, and also complete the 'security question' fields it asks for afterward.
answers.C: Check the web address carefully or type the university's URL in yourself instead of using the link.

explanation: A pixel-perfect copy of your university's login page is exactly what credential phishing looks like - the giveaway is almost always the web address, not the design.
proTip: A login page you reached by typing the address yourself is safer than one a link opened for you.
